findings.title: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE changed from 4 to 3, breaking existing scripts
findings.body: This PR changes RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE from 4 to 3 (and reassigns 4 to FEATURE_DISABLED). Any automation or CI/CD pipeline written against the previous release that branches on exit code 4 to detect 'recreate upgrade required' will now silently misinterpret the result: exit code 4 now means the feature is disabled, and recreate is signaled by a different code. Since the whole point of this tool is to be scriptable via exit codes (as documented), this is a breaking contract change for existing consumers. If the renumbering is intentional, it should at least be called out in the PR description/release notes; alternatively pick an unused code (e.g. 5) for FEATURE_DISABLED to preserve compatibility.

findings.title: testFeatureNotEnabled does not assert the new exit code 4
findings.body: The new test testFeatureNotEnabled only asserts the error message but not the process exit code. The feature-disabled path introduces a new documented exit code (4), which is the primary machine-readable contract of this tool. A regression that prints the message but exits with the wrong code (e.g. 1 or 0) would not be caught. The test should assert result.exitCode() == 4, as the other tests assert exit codes explicitly (e.g. testCompatible asserts 0).

findings.title: CAUTION claims the Operator fails without the rolling-updates feature, but the default strategy is documented as usable
findings.body: The added CAUTION states 'the feature rolling-updates must be enabled. Otherwise, the Keycloak Operator will fail.' However the same section documents that the default (`<not set>`) strategy mimics Keycloak 26.1 or older behavior, and the accompanying UpgradeTest only enables the rolling-updates feature when a strategy is explicitly set (updateStrategy != null). This means the operator does not fail for the default strategy without the feature, contradicting the CAUTION. The doc should clarify that the feature is required only when spec.update is configured (e.g. with an explicit strategy), otherwise users following the doc will enable the feature unnecessarily or distrust the doc after observing the default path works without it.
